text:
A: Hello. Can you hear me?
B: Yes. Hi. I'm Tomasz.
A: Nicola. Sorry, is it Tomasz with a Z?
B: Yes, with a Z at the end. It's Polish.
A: Okay. I'm in Basingstoke. I'm a practice manager at a GP surgery. So I run reception, the admin team, rotas, budgets, complaints. What do you do?
B: Electrician. Domestic and some light commercial. In East London, Walthamstow.
A: Oh, my husband's an electrician. Darren. He's got his own business, him and an apprentice.
B: Okay. Self-employed. That's what I want to do. In two years, maybe.
A: Well, I'll tell you now, to be honest, the paperwork's the bit nobody warns you about. I do Darren's invoices half the time because otherwise they just sit in the van. He's hopeless. He never puts anything back where it goes either.
B: I do my paperwork the same day. I don't like it, but if I leave it, it gets worse.
A: Good. That's exactly right. Erm, what sort of jobs?
B: Rewires, consumer units, EV chargers. And a lot of EICRs, the testing for landlords. That's what I want to focus on, when I go on my own. Testing and EV, maybe solar. I'm looking at a course for solar.
A: Is there money in the landlord testing?
B: Yes. Every five years they need it, by law. So it's steady. Lots of landlords, lots of flats in London.
A: The man I just spoke to does lettings. He'd probably give you work. He's got a colour-coded spreadsheet for every gas certificate.
B: That's good. Most don't. They call you the week before it runs out.
A: Mm. That's my GPs with their appraisals. Everything's last minute and then it's my problem.
B: Yeah.
A: Sorry, I'm going on. I saw your photo, you had all those jars with labels. I thought, that's someone who likes things organised.
B: Yes. My partner laughs. I label circuits at work properly, so at home also, it's habit. My tools are colour-coded.
A: I'd love that. Our kitchen drawer's a disaster. I have the meal plan on the whiteboard on the fridge, you might have seen, and Darren and my son just ignore it. Dinner's at half six, and somebody's always late.
B: I cook most of the dinners in the week. And on Sunday I batch-cook. Soup, chicken and rice for my lunches. I eat in the van.
A: That's sensible. You're saving money doing that. I don't know how anyone affords buying lunch every day now, honestly, the price of everything.
B: Yes. And materials also. Copper has gone up a lot. Cable is much more than three years ago.
A: Darren says that. He complains every time he goes to the wholesaler. Erm, can I ask, did they tell you what this is all for? The calls?
B: No. I think they just want to see how people talk.
A: Right. I just find it a bit odd, three minutes with someone and then a survey. I like to know what the point is.
B: Yeah. It's short. Easy, I think.
A: Well, you're very calm about it. I'm sat here thinking, am I doing it wrong.
B: No, it's fine. Just talking.
